findings.element: The editor's WHEN field and the note beneath it (input#b-edit-date, p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint) - render-b.js commitDate() line 1055-1057 and the stepper's ceilingNote at line 740-744.
findings.problem: Driven on both grounds at 1440x960, owner-editing: type '4 October 2026' into WHEN and press Enter. The entry is refused - aria-invalid goes true, the input border goes from rgba(17,17,17,0.28) to solid ink (rgba(255,255,255,0.28) to solid white on ink) and nothing moves. The words written under the field are 'This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself.' That is the same sentence, in the same 13px Geist 400 at 62% ink, that the surface writes when a date IS accepted at the limit: move the same moment to '3 October 2026' and the note reads identically with aria-invalid false. So one string carries both 'we took it, you are at the edge' and 'we did not take it'. Nothing in the sentence says the entry was not taken, and the field goes on holding the rejected string '4 October 2026' while the readout twenty pixels below still reads 'Saturday 8 August 2026 - in 23 days'. The screen holds two dates and only the border alpha says which one stands. The other two refusals from the same refuse() call are written the other way round and both name the remedy: 'That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026.' and 'That day has gone. Pick one still ahead.' So one refusal in three is in a different grammar from the other two, and it is the only one that shares its words with a non-error state. This is a real path, not a contrivance: a wedding weekend has a next-day brunch, and typing it is the first thing an owner does to find out whether the plan can hold it.
findings.fix: In commitDate (render-b.js:1055), stop reusing the standing sentence for the refusal. Before the guards add `var standing = recordFor(item.getAttribute('data-id')).date;` and replace the over-ceiling branch with `return refuse('Nothing can sit after ' + F.fmt.longYear(F.project.primaryDate.date) + '. Still ' + F.fmt.longYear(standing) + '.');` - it states the rule, states that the entry was not taken, and names the date that still stands, matching the grammar of the other two refusals. Leave 'This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself.' as the standing note written by ceilingNote (render-b.js:741) when away >= ceiling with aria-invalid false, so the two conditions no longer share a string. Extend the clearing guard at render-b.js:729 from /not a date|has gone/ to /not a date|has gone|Nothing can sit after/ so a later valid entry wipes it. Same edit serves both grounds; no colour, weight or structure changes.

findings.element: print, .b-printLink - 'The plan stays online at' plus F.shareUrlFull (render-b.js:1963-1965).
findings.problem: The keepsake's only route to the live plan is 'https://timeline.signalstudio.ie/s/j7Qm2vK4xR9bT1nL6yH3cW8pZ5sD0aG7fJ4uE2rN9tM' - 76 characters ending in a 43-character case-sensitive random token, set in mono and broken across three lines. Nobody can act on that from paper. The sheet is not a private object: it is the thing handed to the venue, the celebrant and the day's helpers on the morning, and those are exactly the people who do NOT already hold the link in a message - the couple and the families got the unfurl card in chat, the venue got a printout. So the one surface with no way to recover is the one that makes the offer, and the label 'The plan stays online at' is an instruction the reader cannot follow. The footer's 'Kept by Orla' means the fallback is to interrupt the person running the day to ask for a link. Every printed artifact in the benchmark set - a Stripe receipt, an event ticket - carries a scannable route for exactly this reason.
findings.fix: BUILD. Render a QR of F.shareUrlFull inside .b-printLink, above the existing URL paragraph, and keep the URL text under it as the human-readable fallback. The token is static, so encode it at build time in build.mjs and emit an inline SVG of black modules on white at about 28mm square - pure ink on paper, so it introduces no hue, no type, no new radius and no new object class, and print already forces the paper ground. Give the SVG role='img' with aria-label 'Scan to open the plan online' so the screen-shown print state still states what it is. Label it in the existing micro register as 'Scan to open it' beside 'The plan stays online at'.

biggestWin: The owner's loop is completely reversible and completely spoken. Driven end to end on both grounds - set a day from empty, add a moment, rename it, move it seven days, hide it from guests, delete it - every one of those commits lands in the same bar in the same place, names the moment and the move in a sentence ('Send the invitations moved 7 days later.', 'Menu tasting at The Orchard is now hidden from guests.', 'Send the invitations was removed.'), and every one of them comes back with Ctrl+Z, delete included, with the row restored and the measure re-laid without losing scroll or focus. Around it the date field refuses three different ways in three human sentences rather than one validation error, normalises what it can ('31 September 2026' becomes 1 October, the field is rewritten and the undo bar says how far it moved), and Enter commits in the first field. The empty state is one question, one field, one button and one example, and it hands focus straight to 'Add a moment' when the day is set. Nothing here needs explaining to someone who has never used a planning tool, and none of it is a frame - it all runs, identically, on paper and on ink.
